newsitem.title: USA: LDC debts mixed in subdued pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: LDC debts mixed in subdued pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Latin Bradies were lightly mixed while East European and Russian papers held on to slightly firmer ground in moderate trade ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving Day holiday.
"The Bradies followed the Treasuries higher earlier on and then came off in profit-taking," said a Brady bond trader, who noted that the spreads of major Latin Bradies widened about 5 basis points.
The slide owed more to Thanksgiving Day holiday and the month-end lethargy than to changes in the economic fundamentals or market sentiments, he said.
The trading volume had dwindled since last week, but some traders expected another burst in December before the market wound down for year-end.

"The buyside is long cash," said another trader. With a calm outlook for the near term, the yields from emerging market debts would draw players into the arena, compared to earning the piddling returns from U.S. money market.
"It pays to stay in the game," he noted.
Argentina FRBs added 1/8 to 85-5/8 bid, while Brazil C eased 1/8 to 72-1/2 bid.

Ecuador papers were among the more actively traded as anticipation for a convertibility plan that would peg the sucre to the U.S. dollar continued to buoy debt prices. The expected pricing of the planned eurobond issue, however, drew widespread skepticism, market sources said.
An Ecuador's government source said the issue would likely to be $400 million, with five-year maturity and priced at 350 basis points over U.S. Treasury.
"The talk of 350 is not very realistic," scoffed a trader, noting that at 350 basis points, Ecuador Par would be barely 25 basis points over Argentina Par, which would be a travesty.
The most Ecuador could aim at would be 375 to 400 basis points, the trader said.
Argentina Pars was unchanged at 63-3/4 bid, while Ecuador Pars was off 1/8 at 47.00 bid.
Omar Borla, Latin America economist at Robert Flemings, Inc., said the impact of the currency convertibility plan had not been carefully thought out.
The stage of development of the Ecuadorian economy is not comparable to the Argentinian when the currency board was introduced, he said.
"It has become more a political decision than an economic decision," Borla said.
Russian and East European debts barely drew any interest in U.S. trading. Russia Minfin 3 added 1/4 to 83-5/8 bid, and Bulgaria FLRB edged 1/8 higher to 36-3/8 bid.
